newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo Nobel details Q2 operations.
newsitem.headline: Akzo Nobel details Q2 operations.

text.p: Folowing is a summary of comments made by chemical group Akzo Nobel NV on the performance of its four main product groups in the second quarter of 1997:

Operating income up on year-ago period, mainly due to higher sales volumes at Organon (prescription drugs), Intervet (animal health) and Diosynth (raw materials for drugs). Organon posted volume gains for contraceptive pills, Remeron (new antidepressant) and Puregon (new fertility drug) but incurred higher costs for product launches and research.

Earnings of all coatings business units improved significantly vs Q2 1996, reflecting higher volumes sold, cost-saving measures and a recovery in margins. Reorganisations in wake of Akzo merger with Nobel in 1994 have left business units in better shape to respond to market developments. CHEMICALS --

Polymer Chemicals did better due to higher volumes. Surface Chemistry earnings rose because of volume growth and cost-saving measures. Catalysts start to reap cost benefits of investment projects. Euro Salt earnings lower due to tougher competition.

Results would seem to have improved with better than expected contribution from Industrial Fibres. However, product group continues to suffer from worldwide capacity surplus which exerts strong pressure on selling prices. Despite many measures taken, operating profit is still barely two percent of sales, not even enough to compensate for financing charges. Akzo Nobel will continue to look for additional measures to improve results of loss-making or barely profitable ativities. On positive note Sympatex (breathing, waterproof textile fibre) and Fortafil (U.S. carbon fibre business) posted adequate results.
